question_text: How much heat must be supplied to 250 g of tungsten to raise its temperature from $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $650^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$? The specific heat of tungsten is $0.032 \frac{\mathrm{cal}}{\mathrm{g} \cdot \mathrm{K}}$.The unit of the answer is cal.
response:
Using the heat equation $Q = mc\Delta T$:

- $m = 250\ \text{g}$
- $c = 0.032\ \frac{\text{cal}}{\text{g}\cdot\text{K}}$
- $\Delta T = 650 - 25 = 625\ \text{K}$

$$Q = (250)(0.032)(625) = 5000\ \text{cal}$$

$$\boxed{5000}$$
